title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset A) — An auditory brain-computer interface based on selective attention to multiple tone streams
description: EEG dataset from 11 healthy participants performing a 3-class auditory brain-computer interface task based on selective attention to three concurrently presented tone streams, exploiting auditory stream segregation. Musical tones were delivered to the right ear, and participants counted targets in the attended stream, eliciting P300 responses. 64-channel EEG and 2-channel EOG were recorded at 1000 Hz, and Riemannian-geometry classification achieved over 80% accuracy for five subjects.
methods_description: Piano tones from a software synthesizer were presented to the right ear through a digital signal processor and headphones. Three streams each contained standard (90%) and deviant (10%) tones, with 150 ms tone duration and 180 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. Each session had two task blocks of three 5-minute runs. 64-channel EEG and 2-channel EOG were recorded at 1000 Hz. Classification used xDAWN spatial filtering and Riemannian geometry with 10-fold cross validation.
